title: Customer Launch Sprint Canvas and Release Communication Orchestration
creator: Maya Srinivasan
description:
Purpose:
This ticket defines the runbook, sprint canvas, and cross-team orchestration required to release a controlled beta to lighthouse customers, coordinate release notes and comms, and close the feedback loop into product and reliability engineering. It ensures we ship a measurable pilot with clear success criteria and a repeatable communication cadence for future launches.

Scope:
- Prepare a 4-week beta pilot for up to 12 lighthouse accounts (mix of AI-native startups and regulated enterprise).
- Coordinate engineering readiness (runtime capacity, observability dashboards, rollback policies).
- Author release notes and triage communications for developer and customer-facing channels.
- Define feedback intake, categorization, severity tagging, and SLAs for follow-up.
- Establish success metrics, escalation paths, and transition criteria from beta -> general availability.

Outcomes / Acceptance Criteria:
- Beta Readiness Checklist green: model pinned, infra autoscaling policy validated, canary traffic plan approved.
- Release notes published in docs with clear breaking changes, migration guidance, and sample SDK snippets.
- 12 lighthouse accounts provisioned and briefed; at least 6 have completed integration smoke tests within first two weeks.
- Feedback pipeline configured: Typeform + dedicated Slack channel + internal Jira/Linear triage queue.
- Observable KPIs instrumented: per-route p50/p95 latency, unit cost per token, error rate, and quality regression score against eval suite.

Timeline & Milestones:
- Week 0 (2026-03-08): Finalize lighthouse list, kickoff cross-functional readiness sync.
- Week 1 (2026-03-15): Engineering completes canary rollout plan; docs team drafts release notes.
- Week 2 (2026-03-22): Lighthouse onboarding begins; observability dashboards live.
- Week 3 (2026-03-29): Collect initial feedback; triage meeting; patch/rollforward if required.
- Week 4 (2026-04-05): Evaluate success criteria; decide GA gate or extended pilot.

Stakeholders & Responsibilities:
- PM (assignee): overall plan, lighthouse selection, success criteria, GTM comms.
- ENG: runtime capacity validation (ENG-24321), canary policy, rollback automation.
- Design: onboarding UX and quickstart flows (DES-8842).
- Docs/DevRel: release notes, migration guide, SDK snippets.
- Support/CS: SLA for ticket response during pilot, customer briefings.
- Security/Compliance: checklist for data residency and KMS integration for any lighthouse requiring Private deployment.

Release Notes / Comms Orchestration:
- Single authoritative release notes doc and changelog entry; include short TL;DR, migration steps, known limitations, and contact path.
- Staged communications: internal RFC -> engineering readiness signoff -> private customer brief -> public developer blog + changelog entry.
- Responsible owners: Docs (primary), PM (review and signoff), Legal (if terminology requires compliance review).
- Timing: release notes must be published 48 hours before any public announcement; customer-specific briefings scheduled 72 hours prior.

Feedback Loop & Triage:
- Intake channels: in-product feedback widget, dedicated survey (Typeform), and customer success notes.
- Triaging: categorize as Quality | Reliability | Feature Request | Docs; tag severity (S1-S4) and target SLAs (S1: 24h, S2: 72h).
- Owner assignment: ENG for S1-S2 reliability/bugs, PM+ENG for quality regressions, Docs for docs issues.
- Closed-loop: quarterly follow-up summary for each lighthouse account with actions and timeline.

KPIs & Success Criteria:
- Adoption: at least 50% of lighthouse accounts complete integration by day 14.
- Reliability: p95 latency within SLA goal for 95% of requests; error rate <0.5% during pilot.
- Cost: per-token unit cost within 20% of projection for >=80% of workload.
- Quality: no critical quality regression in eval suite; customer-reported major quality issues <=2.
- Business signal: at least 3 lighthouse accounts indicate intent to purchase Dedicated or Private in follow-up.

Risk & Mitigation:
- Risk: unexpected tail latency due to batching changes. Mitigation: enable canary to 5% traffic, keep fallback to earlier kernel selection, and monitor KV cache hit rate.
- Risk: customers misinterpret breaking behavior in structured output. Mitigation: explicit migration examples in release notes + quick migration script.
- Risk: support overload during onboarding. Mitigation: pre-schedule office hours, rotate on-call CS+Eng, and provide runbook playbook.

Transition Criteria to GA:
- All acceptance criteria met and signoff from ENG, PM, Security, and Docs.
- No outstanding S1 issues; S2 issues have committed fix timelines.
- GTM assets ready: changelog, migration guide, tutorial video, and sales one-pager.

Next Steps / Action Items:
- [PM] Finalize lighthouse customer list (due 2026-03-05).
- [ENG] Submit canary rollout PR and capacity validation report (ENG-24321) (due 2026-03-12).
- [Docs] Publish draft release notes and sample SDK snippets (due 2026-03-13).
- [CS] Schedule onboarding calls with first 6 lighthouse accounts (due 2026-03-14).
